newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas rises amid SW heat, storage demand.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas rises amid SW heat, storage demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices moved slightly higher Tuesday as aftermarket demand continued to remain firm and hot weather blanketed most of the Southwest, industry sources said.

Louisiana Gulf prices at the Henry Hub gained another two cents to about $2.23-2.26 per mmBtu as temperatures in the Southwest climbed about six to 12 degrees above normal, thereby triggering additional cooling demand.
Similarly in south Texas, prices climbed about three cents to $2.12-2.14.

In the Northeast, New York city-gate prices rose several cents to $2.50-2.58 as cooler-than-normal weather covered the area. Temperatures are expected to continue to drop as the week progresses, falling to five to 10 degrees below normal by the weekend, Weather Services Corp said.
Appalachian prices were up a couple of cents to the low-to-mid $2.40s on Columbia and CNG.
In the Midcontinent, where most temperatures are also hovering below normal, prices firmed by an average of three cents to about $2.01-2.04.
Midcontinent temperatures are also expected to drop further later this week.
Chicago city-gate values were again talked in the low-$2.30s, while Detroit city-gate gas sold at $2.34-2.37.
In west Texas, Permian prices were up three cents to the high-$1.90s, while prices at the southern California border inched two cents higher to about $2.12.
